articles.title_orig: Hamas in talks with Palestinian factions over Israeli targeted killings in Gaza
articles.title_zh: Hamas in talks with Palestinian factions over Israeli targeted killings in Gaza
articles.content_orig:
Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya said that the terrorist organization was holding consultations with other Palestinian factions on how to respond to a recent series of Israeli targeted killings of senior Hamas officials in the Gaza Strip.
“The equation of continued killing and siege under an agreement is unacceptable to us. We are holding discussions with the other Palestinian factions on how to respond to the daily killings directed against us,” al-Hayya said.
Al-Hayya did not specify what measures Hamas and the other Palestinian factions were considering in response to the Israeli strikes.
His remarks came after the IDF and Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) confirmed on Thursday that they had killed senior Hamas political bureau official Khaled Abu Nada in a strike in Deir al-Balah in the central Gaza Strip.
Abu Nada headed Hamas's Economic Department and served as the terrorist organization's education minister. According to the military, he was responsible for managing Hamas's banking and investment systems and directing funds toward terrorist activities and the rehabilitation of its military capabilities.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz said in a joint statement on Thursday that Israel would continue targeting members of Hamas's leadership.
“No terrorist is immune, and no one in the Hamas leadership will manage to evade us,” Netanyahu and Katz said.
On Wednesday, the IDF and Shin Bet confirmed the killing of Muhammad Majed Abu al-Ouf , the head of Hamas's internal security apparatus in the northern Gaza Strip.
According to the military, Abu al-Ouf was involved in efforts to restore Hamas's operational capabilities and had overseen executions of Palestinians who opposed the terrorist organization's rule.
The strike followed the killing of Naeem Abu Nahel , the head of Hamas's internal security apparatus in the Gaza Strip, which Netanyahu and Katz confirmed on Tuesday.
Hamas condemned Abu Nahel's killing and called on the international community to pressure Israel to adhere to the ceasefire agreement.
The targeted killings come amid ongoing international efforts to advance the implementation of US President Donald Trump's peace plan for the Gaza Strip, including the disarmament of Hamas and the establishment of an alternative governing authority.
On Monday, the Board of Peace announced that Hamas and other Palestinian factions had agreed to a disarmament roadmap, providing for the relinquishment of their weapons and the transfer of civilian and security responsibilities to a transitional Palestinian administration.
However, the board acknowledged that implementation remained limited, calling on both Israel and Hamas to fulfill their commitments under the agreement.

Grand Theft Auto 6 developer Rockstar Games has an outdated habit of double-dipping on its customers. First comes a console version , and months later, a PC version arrives . By then, a lot of PC gamers have already bought the game once on console, and they're coerced into buying it again.
I think I bought GTA 5 three times over the years as I moved onto different hardware. This time around, GTA 6 has barely been out for a week on Xbox Series X|S and PS5/Pro , and we already have what appears to be a working version of the game on PC .
Hobbyist developers and AI vibe coders have taken it upon themselves to get unofficial GTA 6 builds pulled from consoles running on Windows PC . You might have already seen it proclaimed on social media that GTA 6 has arrived for PC. That's not quite true. Here's what's actually going on, and what it means (and doesn't mean) for PC gamers.
Shortly after the official GTA 6 console launch on November 19 , hacker Cyberleek — the group behind the bulk of the pre-launch gameplay and content leaks — released some significant portions of the Xbox build.
It wasn't until a couple of days later, when the game's executable file was published, that recompilation efforts for Windows PC really kicked off. Within hours of the executable's release, I saw developers posting proof that the game was launching on PC. A few hours later, they were able to get through the game's initial setup.
Since then, and over the past couple of days, recompilation efforts have really ramped up. Today, at the time of writing, someone has posted a clip on Reddit of GTA 6 running on PC at 60+ FPS .
The Reddit thread I linked, containing the video of GTA 6 running on PC at 60+ FPS, has already been deleted . You'll have to trust me on this one.
That's some incredible progress in a project that barely launched just a couple of days ago. However, it's still a very long way from becoming a finished, stable port that you or I might want to play through.
Running a console version of a game on PC usually requires emulation . An emulator is essentially a live interpreter, allowing your PC to pretend it's a console while it translates instructions.
This extra layer of work usually saps performance in a major way, especially in a game as demanding and complex as GTA 6. With the rise of powerful, personal AI assistants, recompilation has become the new and preferred way for this type of work.
Imagine you're reading a book written in a language you don't understand. Would you rather have a live interpreter telling you what each line means, or would you rather just read the translated version without all the hassle?
Recompilation works the same way, converting the game's code from console-compatible to natively PC-compatible. If it's done properly, the results can be quite astounding. Just look at the Ocarina of Time remake's unofficial PC port that arrived shortly after the game's real launch on Switch 2.
Recompiling a game's code has always been possible , but it was a matter of time and effort that stopped most projects from going live. Now, with the impressive advances in AI coding tools , console-to-PC conversions have become something that practically anyone with enough token budget can take on.
And that's basically what's going on today, with groups of would-be coders assembling their AI agents into swarms to tackle the massive recompilation task.
The entire GTA 6 recompilation fiasco would probably be getting a lot more attention if it weren't totally illegal because of how the game's files are being leaked and distributed. Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two , has been busy shutting down projects like Leonida , one of the leading efforts to recompile GTA 6 on PC.
GitHub has been busy pulling down repositories with game files inside. Still, projects keep popping up en masse, and it's hard to believe that Rockstar will find and shut them all down.
GTA 6 recompilation projects continue, and some are gaining ground at a terrific pace. I still wouldn't expect a polished GTA 6 on PC anytime soon, at least unless Rockstar decides to give us what we want and launch an official version in the coming weeks.
Here's my best advice: no matter how tempting it might be to download a working illegal version of GTA 6 for PC, don't do it .
Not for some moral or legal reasons, though there are plenty, but because there's such a high risk of malware coming in with the files. For now, GTA 6 on PC remains a fascinating push against corporate greed and an example of what AI can really do.

President Donald Trump on Thursday falsely deemed the latest gross domestic product revision a mistake, claiming that it should be "immediately investigated."
Data released Wednesday from the Commerce Department revealed that the U.S. economy exhibited much stronger growth for the third quarter than initially estimated, showing that real GDP grew at a 4.3% annualized rate . That was revised upward from the department's advance estimate of 3.4%.
That revision was a "RECORD SETTING ERROR," Trump said in a Truth Social post , suggesting that the initial release could have influenced the outcome of the 2026 U.S. midterm elections , where Democrats flipped both chambers of Congress and even multiple governorships.
"I would like to wish a Happy Thanksgiving to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%, A RECORD SETTING ERROR, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated," Trump wrote.
However, the difference between the advance estimate and the figure in the second release is far from being an all-time record. It was the largest revision since the 1.2 percentage point revision seen in the second quarter of 2020.
On an absolute basis, the latest revision was tied for 16th among all revisions from the advance estimate to the second release since 1990. It also tied four other quarters with a similar 0.9 percentage point difference — and was approximately double the average revision of 0.43 percentage points for all 147 quarters.
The upward revision shows Trump's policies are "delivering results" that defy expectations, White House spokesman Matthew Middleton told CNBC.
Revisions to U.S. economic numbers are not out of the ordinary . Initial reports count on partial survey data and early estimates. Those data are later updated with more survey responses — which sometimes leads to changes from the initial reports.
GDP data is revised repeatedly over a five year period. By the time the final revision is done, the average absolute error from the second release to the final is 1.14 percentage points.
The advance estimate for Q3 U.S. GDP, which came just days before Election Day in early November, was still better than the figure economists had expected at the time. It also showed a significant step-up in growth from the second quarter.
Because that was a strong showing for the economy, some on Wall Street consider this week's revision to be a confirmation of the economy's recent growth trend.
Jim Baird of Plante Moran Financial Advisors said immediately following the release that it "reinforces an increasingly familiar tension" that the economy is "performing quite well, but its resilience also gives the Fed an even stronger case for further rate hikes."
"The economy isn't merely hanging in there. It continues to demonstrate considerable resilience, with consumers spending, businesses investing and few signs that restrictive monetary policy is creating significant cracks in the broader expansion," the firm's chief investment officer said.
Traders are currently pricing in a nearly 100% chance of a hike at the Federal Open Market Committee's December meeting, per the CME FedWatch tool . They're also anticipating an additional hike in January.
— CNBC's Jeff Cox and Fred Imbert contributed reporting

articles.title_orig: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
articles.title_zh: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia is under pressure to do things differently, and a new WSJ report shows how far that’s going.
According to the Journal, Nvidia has told manufacturing partners, including Dell and Super Micro, to hit pause on server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia for an unspecified period as it assesses whether its regional partners are meeting U.S. export requirements.
As for why those countries, Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers there, a loophole the US Commerce Department closed — reportedly grudgingly —  earlier this month. The Journal notes that the think tank Institute for Progress estimates remote data centers like these supply about 24% of China’s AI computing power.

articles.title_orig: Amtrak ridership hits record as high gas prices drive more Americans to train travel
articles.title_zh: Amtrak ridership hits record as high gas prices drive more Americans to train travel
articles.content_orig:
Historic growth, new trains and generational infrastructure investments and improvements strengthen Amtrak’s future for its biggest transformation yet
WASHINGTON – Amtrak travelers took a record 37.1 million customer trips in Fiscal Year (FY) 2026, achieving 7.4% ridership growth – Amtrak’s largest annual increase in more than a decade outside the pandemic recovery years. Also, for the first time in company history, total operating revenue passed $4 billion, allowing Amtrak to invest even more to improve the customer experience and modernize stations, trains and infrastructure. It’s Amtrak’s third straight year of record-breaking performance and reflects the growing demand for passenger rail.
“We aren’t just saying it’s a ‘New Era of Rail’ at Amtrak, we are proving it,” said Amtrak Interim President Byl Herrmann . “More customers chose Amtrak than ever before, generating record revenue while reinforcing the essential role passenger rail plays in connecting communities and supporting economic growth all across the country.”
“This year proved what we’ve believed for a long time: when you invest in passenger rail, Americans show up,” said Amtrak Board Chair Tony Coscia. “New trains, stronger infrastructure and better stations are bringing more people on board than ever before, and we’re just getting started in providing them with a world-class experience.”
The year closed with a defining milestone: the debut of Airo trains on the Amtrak Cascades route in the Pacific Northwest. The Airo launch continues the fleet modernization that will elevate travel across the Amtrak network.
A better customer experience and more NextGen Acela service all helped Amtrak meet historic demand for passenger rail in the United States, as did safe, reliable service during landmark events including the FIFA World Cup TM and America’s 250 th birthday.
Amtrak is in the midst of a historic service overhaul and fleet expansion. In the last year, Secretary Duffy and the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) invested $465.8 million in federal funding to overhaul the customer experience at Washington Union Station, put over $200 million towards the revitalization of New York’s Penn Station, and awarded Amtrak $2.05 billion to acquire 43 Made-in-America trainsets to replace Amtrak’s aging fleet, among other milestones.
“Under President Trump and his Golden Age of Rail initiative, Amtrak is setting records like never before and we’re not slowing down. In the new year, we’ll break ground on New York’s brand new Penn Station and choose a project manager to spearhead Washington Union Station’s revitalization,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy . “We’ve also been able to invest billions into Amtrak in 2026 after cutting the cord on California’s Train to Nowhere. Instead of wasting taxpayer dollars on boondoggles, we’re helping Amtrak add new trainsets and open new routes across the U.S. to improve passenger experience and make rides safer and more affordable for American families. I’m grateful to Amtrak and their incredible partnership in achieving these feats for the American people.”
Preliminary results for FY26 (Oct. 2025 – Sept. 2026) include:
Keeping America Connected FY26 showcased the essential role Amtrak plays in connecting communities and moving the nation during major moments. From supporting travel tied to the FIFA World Cup 2026™ and America’s 250th anniversary celebration to serving record holiday travel, Amtrak helped millions of customers reach the events, destinations, and experiences that matter most. Strong demand across the network reinforced rail’s growing role in America’s transportation future.
A Better Travel Experience Customer-focused investments enhanced the journey at every stage of travel. Amtrak introduced new onboard dining options, expanded premium offerings, improved station experiences, and continued investing in cleaner trains and facilities. Growing loyalty program engagement, innovative partnerships, and new brand campaigns helped strengthen customer connections while reinforcing Amtrak’s position as a preferred mode of travel.
A New Generation of Trains FY26 marked significant progress in modernizing America’s passenger rail fleet. NextGen Acela continued redefining high-speed rail travel on the Northeast Corridor, surpassing key ridership milestones while expanding schedules as 16 trains have entered service. At the same time, the Airo fleet advanced from testing to deployment, with the first two Amtrak Cascades trainsets launching in the Pacific Northwest and the remaining trainsets, now fully manufactured, preparing to enter service. The first Northeast Regional trainset began testing and commissioning. Together, these steps move the fleet toward full Amtrak Cascades deployment and future service on the Northeast Corridor.
Building for the Next Century Amtrak continued advancing the largest infrastructure program in its history, delivering progress on major bridge, tunnel, station, rail yard, and maintenance facility projects nationwide. Critical investments along the Northeast Corridor and beyond improved reliability, increased capacity, and strengthened the long-term resilience of the network. From the Portal North Bridge and East River Tunnel to maintenance facilities and station renovations, these projects are laying the foundation for future growth.
Investments in People, Safety and Accessibility Amtrak remained committed to creating a safer, more accessible railroad. The company delivered improvements across key safety metrics, expanded accessibility upgrades at stations nationwide, and advanced its goal of achieving full ADA accessibility across the network.
Looking Ahead With strong ridership demand, major infrastructure projects underway, a modernizing fleet, and a continued focus on safety, accessibility, and customer service, Amtrak is entering its next chapter from a position of strength. The company remains committed to delivering a world-class passenger rail experience while expanding opportunity, enhancing reliability, and building a stronger national network for future generations.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft: Salt Typhoon’s ARTEX wins access ‘in a matter of minutes’
articles.title_zh: Microsoft: Salt Typhoon’s ARTEX wins access ‘in a matter of minutes’
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft logo at the Microsoft Experience Center, New York
State-backed hacking groups from China and North Korea, including Salt Typhoon, have added the AI attack framework ARTEX to their tools, Microsoft says. Microsoft Threat Intelligence named the groups in a report published on Wednesday .
The list covers Crystal Typhoon and Salt Typhoon, two Chinese state groups, and Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet, which Microsoft tracks as North Korean. Two more clusters, Storm-0940 and Storm-3358, are also on it. Microsoft says state-sponsored and financially motivated hackers use ARTEX to speed up network scans, credential attacks, and attacks on web apps.
“Depending on the threat actor’s configuration and the target’s defenses, ARTEX can advance from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access to a target organization in a matter of minutes,” Microsoft wrote.
The report landed hours after US media tied ARTEX to the hack of three US spy agencies , as Jonathan Greig reported for The Record .
US agencies believe Salt Typhoon breached at least nine telecoms groups in 2024, The Record noted. That hack allegedly reached phones used by Donald Trump and JD Vance. A US House report later said Chinese carriers were still inside American phone networks .
Crystal Typhoon is newer. It was first seen in late 2023 and goes after government networks and critical infrastructure through edge devices and firewalls, TechRadar reported .
Microsoft had already linked Storm-0940 to the ConnectWise supply chain attack . The new report adds numbers from its campaigns. In one, Microsoft logged more than 151,000 failed sign-ins, peaking at 2,900 a minute. In several intrusions, the attackers had privileged access less than three hours after they first went after a target.
In another case, an AI agent went from searching GitHub for client secrets to taking data from Azure Key Vault in five minutes.
A GitHub user called Autumn-27 published ARTEX as open-source code with a Chinese interface in July. The developer took it down in October, but other developers kept publishing their own versions. This month, the Chinese security firm ThreatBook claimed ownership and started selling access to “ARTEX Pro”.
The attacker sets the targets. One AI model breaks the job into goals. A planner agent then hands short tasks to worker agents with a real shell and hacking tools. A reporter agent writes up what worked. ARTEX can run on almost any large language model, including ones stripped of their guardrails. That means no single AI provider’s safety controls can stop it, Microsoft says.
The FBI warned about ARTEX earlier this month.
“ARTEX does not introduce new attack techniques; it uses common, pre-existing penetration testing tools and techniques,” Microsoft wrote.
Attackers can change the tool’s IP addresses and user agent strings, so blocking those alone will not work. The steadiest sign is behaviour: many varied requests in a short burst, and quick moves to the next step. ARTEX does nothing to hide that activity by default.
Microsoft also suggests honeypots, tarpits, and fake wins. A fake win shows the agent false proof that its job is done, so it stops. It recommends rate limits, phishing-resistant multifactor sign-in, and replacing any secret that leaks into code. The report also points customers to Microsoft’s own products, including Defender XDR and its Perception security agents.

articles.title_orig: An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs
articles.title_zh: An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs
articles.content_orig:
Megan covers the intersection of science and society. How is biomedical research funded? Who benefits? And how do new technologies reflect and shape our values? You can reach Megan on Signal at mmolteni.13.
Around the world, people are increasingly choosing to have babies later in life for reasons both social and economic. As they get older though, they face a mounting biological challenge: genetic errors caused by chromosomes failing to separate correctly. This phenomenon, known as aneuploidy, is the leading cause of age-related infertility, failed in-vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles, and miscarriage, and it increases dramatically around the age of 40. Studies have shown that between 50% and 80% of embryos from women in their 40s carry chromosomal abnormalities.
One of the main drivers of aneuploidy is the loss of a protein complex called cohesin, which acts like a molecular glue holding chromosomes together. In a new study, researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences in Göttingen, Germany, engineered a novel protein system capable of restoring normal chromosome connections in aging mouse eggs. The study, published Thursday in Science , raises the possibility of one day developing such a system into a treatment that could reduce aneuploidy in human eggs used for IVF.
“There is still work ahead, but their proof of concept was highly successful,” said Rajiv McCoy, a biologist at Johns Hopkins University who was not involved in the work. McCoy’s lab is focused on pregnancy loss, the leading cause of which is aneuploidy. It is estimated that about half of all human conceptions are lost before birth, including the roughly 15% of known pregnancies that end in miscarriage. Technologies that could reduce the odds of miscarriage and expand women’s biological reproductive windows by addressing aneuploidy would have far-reaching consequences for the IVF industry and for society at large. “The stakes are very high,” McCoy said.
When a cell prepares to divide, its chromosomes replicate, forming two copies, or sister chromatids, that are all lined up and organized by a cellular winch system known as the spindle. Within the spindle, the sister chromatids are tethered to each other by cohesin — its ring-like structure traps DNA from both sisters inside it. In most cells, cohesin only has to do this work for a few hours before other enzymes cleave it apart, freeing the chromatids to separate into two new cells. But in oocytes, cohesin has to keep this bond going for decades.
That’s because female babies are born with all the oocytes they will ever have. And already at birth, those 1 to 2 million immature egg cells have begun to divide, and the cohesin’s job is only finished when fertilization occurs. That triggers the end of the division process called meiosis in which the egg cells eject half their genetic material so they can fuse with sperm to make an embryo.
Over all that time, the cohesin molecule doesn’t seem to be reloaded, said Melina Schuh, a director at the Max Planck Institute who led the new work.
For the last two decades, Schuh has been finding new ways of peering into egg cells to better understand how meiosis works and what happens when it goes awry. In 2015, her lab showed for the first time how the structures holding chromosomes together deteriorate in human eggs as they age . Not long after, Schuh began to wonder if they might be able to engineer a system of proteins that could step in and stabilize the chromosomes in older eggs. Over the last eight years, her team tested many different designs before settling on one that did everything they wanted it to.
Called TALhesins, the proteins are designed to attach to specific DNA regions near the centers of each chromosome, tethering them together. The research team also baked a deactivation switch into the TALhesin system —based on cohesin’s natural cleavage sites — so that it would automatically release the chromosomes only when fertilization occurs. In experiments with eggs from older mice, the team found that the TALhesin system reduced premature chromosome separation, increasing the proportion of eggs with properly connected chromatids from 47% to 74% — a level comparable to that found in young mice.
Schuh told STAT her lab has already taken the next step of adapting the TALhesin system to bind to chromosomes in human eggs. “We have initial signs that there is a positive effect on cohesion,” she said. “But what we have not done yet is to really test in human oocytes whether we can reduce errors by stabilizing the chromosomes.”
That’s a critical next step, said Eva Hoffman, a molecular geneticist at the University of Copenhagen, who was not involved in the work. After that, researchers would need to establish that this method for reducing aneuploidy doesn’t introduce other kinds of problems. “The clinical potential depends upon regulatory aspects including safety studies for embryonic development,” Hoffman said. Even with the long road ahead, she commended the German group for generating data that challenges the conventional view of aneuploidy as a condition impossible (or impractical) to intervene in. “Since cohesion is established during fetal life and has to be maintained for decades, its depletion over time was thought to be irreversible,” Hoffman said.
Efforts to address age-related ovarian infertility are long overdue. For older women struggling to get pregnant, currently the only solution that’s available to most patients is to try IVF over and over. (For women between 35 and 40, the odds of getting pregnant are about one in three IVF cycles; for women over 40 it drops to one in ten.) This is both expensive and inefficient, and online support groups are overflowing with heart-wrenching stories of women spending a fortune and years of their lives on failed fertility sagas.
Many clinics also offer a panoply of “add-ons” — experimental treatments with shaky scientific backing — to boost the odds of having a baby. Some clinics overseas have even begun to market mitochondrial replacement techniques (MRT), a controversial method for reducing the risk of mitochondrial disease transmission, as a potential solution for age-related ovarian infertility. A recent STAT investigation found that hundreds of women in their late 30s and 40s have traveled to clinics in the Ukraine, Albania, and other parts of the world seeking MRT to boost the odds of IVF, despite scant evidence that it can overcome issues of aneuploidy.
Schuh has co-founded a startup, Ovo Labs, in Munich and London that has licensed TALhesin from the Max Planck Institute and is trying to commercialize the technology. A key hurdle is that most eggs retrieved in IVF have already undergone the first meiotic division, so cohesin loss could have already caused chromosome errors that can no longer be fixed. While retrieving and treating immature eggs appears to prevent some of these earlier errors, this then requires maturation of eggs in lab dishes, which is not widely used and has its own drawbacks , including that many eggs fail to mature successfully. Shuh is hopeful they can establish a system where oocytes are removed and treated a bit earlier — during the first phase of meiosis — which would require less time and fewer steps to mature.
Ovo Labs has competition from a U.K.-based startup called U-Ploid, co-founded by Schuh’s Max Planck colleague and study co-author, Alexandre Webster. U-ploid’s approach is slightly different, designed to preserve a cell’s natural structures for keeping chromosomes together.
Its lead candidate, Lyvanta, is injected into immature eggs prior to IVF.
Last month, at the 2026 meeting of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine, U-Ploid reported results from a study using immature eggs donated by patients at six U.K. fertility clinics. The study found that 65.5% of eggs treated with Lyvanta matured without detectable chromosome errors, compared to 35.7% of untreated eggs in a control

articles.title_orig: Ubisoft Wants Rayman To Become A Huge, Transmedia Star
articles.title_zh: Ubisoft Wants Rayman To Become A Huge, Transmedia Star
articles.content_orig:
Ubisoft is gearing up to launch Rayman Legends Retold , a reimagined remake of the 2013 original . While many have questioned the decision to remake a game that arguably still looks and plays great to this day, the developers have been clear in their intention to use Retold as a launchpad for the future of the franchise.
Now, in a new interview with The Game Business , brand producer Loïc Gounon has expressed much broader ambitions for the character, perhaps bringing Rayman more in line with something like Sonic in terms of visibility.
In other words, Gounon is thinking about not only games, but other mediums too, including TV shows and comics. The first step is to ensure the brand's success in regions such as the US and Asia, with previous Rayman titles' success being largely limited to Europe.
Subscribe to Nintendo Life on YouTube 856k
“I would like to see Rayman as a must-have IP for video games across the world. Rayman was generally stronger in France and the UK, and in some cases in the US. Enlarging the reach of the IP, also towards Asia and performing well in the US, is the first ambition… making sure that we are a must-have platforming adventure title across those markets in the video game world.
“And I guess beyond the video game world. So, comics, TV series... actually, there’s a French comic book that came out with Rabbids and Rayman being reconnected.”
However, Gounon does not necessarily believe that producing a new 3D title is the key to success, and instead wants to focus on the characters and lore. Sorry to those hoping for Rayman 4 – hey, it might still happen!
“Rayman is iconic because of its gameplay. But going back to the adventure roots of Rayman, having people dive into those characters, exploring deeper into that world and mythology, that’s what we believe in.
“It’s the world-building part, the consistency of that world-building, and the empathy for those characters, that will make the franchise last and maybe become bigger.”
Rayman Legends Retold is right around the corner, scheduled to launch on 3rd December 2026 . Meanwhile, Ubisoft itself is currently coming under fire for its heavy focus on generative AI , with a new report revealing that employees are required to justify reasons for not using the technology in new project pitches.

articles.title_orig: Magyar meets Zelenskyy: Hungary and Ukraine make a fresh start after the icy relations of the Orban era
articles.title_zh: Magyar meets Zelenskyy: Hungary and Ukraine make a fresh start after the icy relations of the Orban era
articles.content_orig:
Magyar shared the story in a post on X , Ukrinform reports.
According to Magyar, Zelensky presented him with an August 1942 issue of the Transcarpathian weekly Az Őslakó (“The Native”).
The Hungarian prime minister said he had often spoken about his great-grandfather, Lajos Eryős, who served as chief notary of Oroszvég during World War II. The former village, known in Ukrainian as Rosvyhovo, is now part of Mukachevo.
The issue contained an announcement of his great-grandfather’s appointment to the post. Magyar said the gesture held special significance within the context of diplomatic protocol.
“Needless to say, a personal gift of this kind has special significance in diplomatic protocol,” Magyar wrote.
On behalf of the Hungarian people, Magyar presented Zelensky with a painting of Mukachevo Castle by Attila Kopriva, a Hungarian-born Transcarpathian artist, and a book by Kyiv-based artist, restorer, and researcher Árpád István Magyar, also known as Stefan-Arpad Yosypovych Magyar. The book is titled Hungarians in Kyiv: From the 9th Century to the Present — Chapters in the History of Hungarian-Ukrainian Relations.
As reported, Magyar arrived in Zakarpattia on November 24 for his first visit to Ukraine as prime minister. In Uzhhorod, he and Zelensky laid flowers at the memorial to fallen Ukrainian defenders on the Hill of Glory.

articles.title_orig: Net Migration to U.K. Falls to Lowest Level Since 1997, Excluding Pandemic
articles.title_zh: Net Migration to U.K. Falls to Lowest Level Since 1997, Excluding Pandemic
articles.content_orig:
Sam Ashworth-Hayes is a former Assistant Comment Editor and leader writer for The Telegraph. He is a political commentator and economist known for his data-driven analysis of British policy, migration, and the "managerial class".
Sixteen years, six prime ministers, and 5.322 million net arrivals since David Cameron promised to lower net migration to the tens of thousands, and his target has finally been hit. The latest figures show 77,000 more people came to Britain than left, the lowest total outside the pandemic since 1997. Victory, at last, for the beleaguered British voter.
At least, that’s the message Labour is keen to project. But while Shabana Mahmood and Andy Burnham are taking credit for restoring “control” of our borders, the data shows something different.
The Government hasn’t brought down migration by removing people who arrived on small boats, or by clamping down on the Boriswave . Instead, three things are going on. The first is that people who arrived under the Conservatives are coming to the end of their visas. While many are applying to stay, some are leaving, meaning that emigration has slowly ticked up over the last few years. The second is that the numbers arriving have fallen as changes have kicked in. And the third is that we’re becoming less British.
That net migration figure of 77,000 includes net inflows of 258,000 non-EU nationals, outflows of 44,000 EU nationals – and another net outflow of 137,000 Britons.
When the term “melting pot” was coined to describe America in 1908, the US foreign-born population was around 13.5 million, or a little less than 15 per cent of the total population of 92 million. Around 3.7 million of this total had arrived from the United Kingdom, Ireland, and Canada: countries with a shared cultural heritage.
Britain is now almost 20 per cent foreign-born, with its population drawn from a wild array of countries. Despite a smaller population overall, we have a larger foreign population than America did when it was the world’s poster-child for rapid demographic upheaval. For voters who want to see the pace of cultural change slow down, there’s little to celebrate here.
And for voters who want economic good news, there’s another issue. Britain’s problem with immigration was never just a matter of quantity. It was also an issue of quality.
Of the 579,000 long-term visas handed out in the last year – excluding visitors and temporary workers – just 48,000, or one in 12, went to main applicants on worker visas. That’s slightly less than arrived through “Refugee Family Reunion” or Partner routes (50,000).
The skilled workers who are coming to Britain are fiscally positive. But as the Migration Advisory Committee has helpfully pointed out , each person arriving on the partner route costs us £109,000 over their lifetimes. If Refugee Family Reunion is similar – and given the extremely poor economic outcomes of refugees in Britain, “similar” is a very conservative assumption – then these groups alone will cost us around £5.4bn over their lifetimes.
If you take the average British 18-year-old and count up their total future fiscal contributions – netting out their pension and healthcare, adding in their taxes paid – then you get to a lifetime value of around £167,000. These 50,000 arrivals will cost us the total lifetime contributions of 33,000 British taxpayers.
Despite this, the sum fiscal contribution of last year’s migration is probably positive. But any benefit is driven almost entirely by that group of roughly 50,000 workers. The other 529,000 people aren’t necessary to reap the benefits, while contributing to our issues with housing shortages and crowded transport. A more selective system would save us billions, massively alleviate infrastructure pressure, and see net migration dip significantly negative as we unwind the Boriswave.
That this is possible is made painfully clear by looking at the British people leaving. Other countries are not competing for our benefits claimants and retirees. By my estimate, based on net flows by age, the Brits who left have taken with them a total lifetime contribution of £12bn to the Treasury.
That, to be clear, is a conservative assessment that assumes “average” careers. But people who emigrate aren’t average. Look at the latest data released and you can find 15,000 Britons on high-skilled visas moving to Australia, 11,000 to the United States, 3,000 to Canada, and another 4,000 to the EU. These are people who are selected for being economically valuable. In the case of Australia, we can see some of the jobs they’ll be doing, and they include over 1,400 doctors and nurses, 300 police officers, and 280 engineers and technicians.
More from Sam Ashworth-Hayes
If the British people we’ve lost are more like the skilled workers who came here, then the cost is more like £21bn. Thanks to research published by the Government , we also know that the foreign nationals who leave tend to be those who earn the highest wages, while those who stay tend to be relatively poor. Add together the net benefits from the migration inflow, and the cost of the outflow, and it is quite likely that we’ve managed to make the population larger and poorer at the same time. Not quite the story Labour was trying to tell.
Sam Ashworth-Hayes is director of research at Reform UK

articles.title_orig: Lawmakers Seek AI Oversight, Tighter China Chip Controls
articles.title_zh: Lawmakers Seek AI Oversight, Tighter China Chip Controls
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia chip sellers are seeking new buyers for the semiconductor giant's hardware, three people told CNBC, after the Trump administration tightened rules to curb Chinese companies' remote access to the most advanced artificial-intelligence systems.
Companies have put an unusually high volume of Nvidia graphics processing units, or GPUs, on the market since new measures restricting Chinese companies renting access to advanced Nvidia chips were announced on Nov. 16, the people said.
Jack Duhamel, president of AI infrastructure marketplace GPU Mart, and two people familiar with the matter told CNBC the surge in GPUs for sale was directly attributable to the new rule. Duhamel added that one company looking to sell Nvidia chips told GPU Mart the sale was related to the new rule.
The two people said it appeared chip sellers were seeking to offload them because they were originally for use in data centers in which Chinese companies would rent access. They asked not to be named because they were discussing private information.
The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, announced an interim final rule as part of a clampdown on Chinese companies bypassing export controls, which effectively ban the sale of the most advanced Nvidia chips to China, by accessing them remotely in overseas data centers. The rule came into effect on Nov. 19.
Deals to find buyers for thousands of B300 GPUs, one of Nvidia's most advanced offerings, have been floated since the rule was announced, said Duhamel and one of the people.
Nvidia declined to comment. BIS did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Nvidia has been facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips.
The chip giant warned its customers that the proposed Remote Access Security Act — which has passed the House of Representatives but is yet to pass the Senate — would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services, potentially exposing both parties to "legal action," sources previously told CNBC.
In July, the U.S. accused a Chinese AI lab, Moonshot AI , of accessing Nvidia chips via a facility in Thailand. CNBC reported on Nov. 5 that the company had sought access to the chips via data centers in Europe.
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday that the new rule announced last week was intended to close "loopholes."
"For a long time, we have not allowed the sale of Blackwell chips, which are the highest AI chips or similar chips to China directly," he said.
"Some rules were issued by the Commerce Department last week to close off indirect access, either smuggling through places like Southeast Asia or remote access from data centers in third countries."
During Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 17, then-interim CEO Colette Kress said the company was still studying the controls, but expected performance to remain strong because demand for chips far exceeded supply.

articles.title_zh: Dominion Energy crews working to restore outages, repair damages caused by storm
articles.content_orig:
• Beast in the East: A massive Thanksgiving storm that spans from Missouri to Massachusetts has knocked out power for more than 900,000 customers , flooded coastal communities and shut down some East Coast bridges and roadways . Water rose to record highs on the Mid-Atlantic coast , and snow blanketed parts of the Midwest before shifting south.
• Air travel snags: Hundreds more flights have been canceled or delayed today after weather disrupted the busy pre-Thanksgiving travel period . Here’s what to do if your flight is delayed.
• Parade paused: The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed for the first time in its history. Americans who enjoy the tradition on TV will have to wait until Saturday, while New Yorkers made the most of the unusually empty streets this morning.
Heavy rain and strong winds hit the East Coast Thursday, putting a snag in some Americans’ Thanksgiving Day plans .
Trees came down onto houses and cars in Washington D.C., Maryland and elsewhere, prompting first responders to rescue motorists and evacuate residents.
Drivers tried to make their way through streets filled with floodwaters in New Jersey, and gusty winds battered pedestrians in New York City, where the iconic Macy’s parade was postponed due to the weather.
Thanksgiving may have just gotten more stressful for hundreds of thousands of Americans as a storm sweeps across the Midwest and East Coast, causing power outages .
Thanksgiving may have just gotten a bit more stressful for more than 850,000 Americans as a storm sweeps across the Midwest and East Coast causing power outages.
The Federal Aviation Administration has issued a ground stop for Delta Air Lines flights headed to New York’s LaGuardia Airport until 7:30 p.m. ET.
Carrier-requested ground stops are often used by airlines to pause incoming aircraft so they can avoid traffic jams and get caught up with the planes already on the ground.
An earlier ground stop for all flights heading to Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport was canceled after about an hour when the FAA reported its objectives had been met.
Meanwhile, an elevated monorail connecting the terminals at Newark Liberty International Airport was shut down due to concerns over high winds . Buses will replace the Air Train, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey said.
And in Miami, a FedEx McDonnell Douglas MD-11 cargo plane that skidded off the runway has been removed, the FAA reported in an operations update. That runway has been out of service since the incident, causing some delays.It should reopen within 48 hours, the agency said.
Floodwaters in Atlantic City, New Jersey, are starting to recede after the storm brought major flooding Thursday, the city’s emergency management coordinator said.
“Things are winding down in the city, although we are still experiencing some water in the streets,” Scott Evans said in a video posted to the city government’s Facebook page . “But the city is in the de-watering process, and the city is draining.”
Some low-lying areas had close to 2 to 3 feet of water, Evans said. Emergency crews helped residents evacuate several homes and carried out more than 14 rescues involving vehicles stuck in deep water, he said.
“We were in major flooding today, so there is some damage out there,” Evans said, adding that officials will assess the damage soon. “We didn’t see the highest levels that we thought we might see, but the the potential was there.”
Some roads are still closed but are expected to reopen in the coming hours.
The East Coast storm continues to take shape this evening, centered just off the Mid-Atlantic coast. Snow has blanketed parts of the Midwest and Ohio Valley while heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding pushed into the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast.
East Coast: Heavy rain and gusty winds are in full force across the Northeast but are beginning to taper across the Mid-Atlantic, though a few showers could linger into the evening. Conditions are deteriorating in New England and will reach their worst overnight.
Another round of coastal flooding will arrive as high tide approaches but, for most areas, won’t be as extreme.
🌧️ Get your local forecast and more in the CNN Weather app ☔️
Midwest: Snow has almost entirely tapered off in Missouri and Illinois after significant snow fell overnight Wednesday, though rain still lingers. Parts of southeast Missouri, western Kentucky and western Tennessee will continue to see a mixed bag of rain and snow through this afternoon. A few inches of snow has already fallen in parts of eastern Tennessee. Wet conditions will begin to taper off this evening.
Great Lakes and Ohio Valley: Rain and wintry precipitation is ongoing from central Tennessee to central Michigan. In parts of central and northern Tennessee, rain has transitioned to wet snow and a few inches will accumulate as temperatures drop . Rain and snow will persist into Friday evening, tapering off overnight.
An ice arena was damaged during a winter storm in the city of Wentzville, Missouri, about 40 miles west of St. Louis, the city said .
The area received major snowfall Wednesday night into Thanksgiving Day.
The arena is closed until further notice while the damage is assessed, the mayor said.
As heavy rain and fierce wind continues to lash the Mid-Atlantic Coast, officials in several Virginia cities say emergency response teams have rescued people from high waters.
Norfolk Fire-Rescue crews performed 39 rescues as of 3:15 p.m. Thursday, a city spokesperson told CNN in a statement. Nearby Virginia Beach has also seen damage from the storm .
There were no injuries related to the water rescues, the spokesperson added. Two dogs were also rescued. The city previously said one person rescued was taken to the hospital, but later said the hospitalization was due to an unrelated incident.
Rising waters have also led to rescues in Poquoson, Virginia, a coastal city about 35 miles north of Norfolk. Around five people had been rescued from their homes as of about 3:15 p.m., according to the city’s fire chief, Mike Bryant.
No injuries were reported, Bryant said, and individuals were all taken to homes of family members less affected by the flooding.
This post has been updated with more information.
CNN’s Brynn Gingras spoke to tourists who came to New York for the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade that has been postponed until Saturday due to weather.

Though family and friends across the country are still feasting on Thanksgiving dinner (or in a post-meal food coma), a storm that could disrupt weekend travel plans across the country is already taking shape.
A weather system that’s set to bring even more rain and snow to the Pacific Northwest Friday night will dive south into the central US, spreading snow across the central Rockies.
The storm will then bring wet weather to the central Plains and Midwest Saturday afternoon and evening.
But the real trouble is likely to set in Sunday morning — typically the busiest travel day of the year — as the storm intensifies and brings the potential of heavy rain and gusty winds from the Louisiana Gulf Coast to southern Michigan.
The system will quickly scoot east and could complicate travel across the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic Sunday afternoon. Evening travel is going to cut it close in the Northeast as the storm swiftly approaches late in the day Sunday.
A second, stronger storm will also approach the West Coast Saturday night, likely impacting travel from eastern Washington to the Bay Area. Rain could spread as far south as Southern California.

articles.title_orig: Spanish economist to become new European Central Bank chief
articles.title_zh: Spanish economist to become new European Central Bank chief
articles.content_orig:
The president of the European Council says eurozone member states have agreed to recommend Pablo Hernandez de Cos as the new European Central Bank (ECB) president.
Antonio Costa also announced that Laurence Boone and Markus Brunnermeier have been recommended as members of the ECB executive board, and noted that this paves the way for the formal appointment of the new European Central Bank leadership by December’s European Union summit.
Pablo Hernandez de Cos will become the first Spaniard to take the role, and succeeds France’s Christine Lagarde at the Frankfurt-based institution at a challenging time for the eurozone.
Currently head of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), the Basel-based forum for the world’s major central banks, the 55-year-old will take over in February, when Lagarde would step down several months before her term expires in October next year.
Thursday’s green light triggers a formal process during which European leaders will later in the day approve the candidates for each ECB post. The bank’s governing council and European Parliament will then formally back the nominations.
Diplomats have described the Spanish economist as a “steady hand” to steer the institution, with a reputation for pragmatism and consensus-building.
As the Bank of Spain’s chief economist and later governor, he navigated the aftermath of Spain’s 2010s banking crisis, years of ultra-low inflation, COVID-19 and the 2022 inflation surge that followed the pandemic and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.
He also chaired the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, the global standard-setter for banks.
Spain’s Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who is battling unfavourable polling before a general election on Sunday, hailed the choice on social media, saying it reflects “a Spain that leads in Europe”.
He pointed to the Spanish chief of the European Investment Bank, Nadia Calvino, and the EU executive’s second-most senior official, Teresa Ribera, as other figures of influence.

articles.title_orig: Sweden's Centre leader backs right-wing prime minister, in major shift
articles.title_zh: Sweden's Centre leader backs right-wing prime minister, in major shift
articles.content_orig:
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson is closing in on a coalition deal to return for another term as head of government, according to three people aware of coalition talks.
The center-right leader, whose party came in second place in September elections, has struck a deal on a political platform with three other parties in view of forming a government, according to the party officials and diplomats.
The Swedish parliament will vote on Kristersson’s potential reappointment as prime minister on Monday.
“Hour by hour we are getting closer to an EPP-led government in Sweden. On Monday the Parliament will vote and hopefully approve Ulf Kristersson as PM,” said Tomás Tobé, European People’s Party vice chair in the European Parliament and party colleague of Kristersson.
Kristersson’s coalition would not have a majority in parliament and would rely on support from other parties to pass legislation. The far-right Sweden Democrats party previously backed Kristersson’s government but has not said it would support him this time.
A crucial factor is whether the Center Party decides to join the coalition. Previously, the party has resisted joining out of opposition to cooperation with the Sweden Democrats.
“The Center Party is on the verge of abandoning what was arguably its most important and powerful election promise: never to enable the Sweden Democrats to wield political influence,” said a Swedish party official aware of the talks. They were granted anonymity, like others in this article, to discuss the sensitive negotiations.
Following reports that the Center Party has taken a preliminary decision to join a four-way coalition government, Kristersson said “there was no alternative to a minority government … it won’t be easy but it isn’t always easy to be in government.”
Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson won the election in September but has since failed to reach a parliamentary majority. Andersson’s failed attempts at forming a government dealt a heavy blow to the EU’s Socialists, which after Sunday’s election in Spain could also lose Pedro Sánchez to a right-wing coalition.
That would leave them with two out of 27 leaders — Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Malta’s Robert Abela.
Swedish parties have been negotiating for 73 days to form a government following an election in September.
This article has been updated with comments from Kristersson.

articles.title_orig: Spain general election 2026: polls, Sanchez vs Feijoo and what happens next
articles.title_zh: Spain general election 2026: polls, Sanchez vs Feijoo and what happens next
articles.content_orig:
Andalusia, Spain – Surrounded by shelves heaving with canned goods and cured meats, the owners of a family-run grocery store are locked in a debate about Spain’s upcoming elections.
All politicians are “liars”, proclaims 32-year-old Antonio Cerezo, announcing he will cast a blank ballot. His cousin, Patricia Nicolas Cerezo, 43, is less certain, riddled with doubt about who to support.
As for her 18-year-old son, first-time voter Alfonso Duque, the only choice is the far-right Vox party : “It can’t get worse than this”.
The one thing that the family in the small village of Rioja seems to agree on is that Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s socialists must go.
A former socialist bastion, the southern region’s political landscape has changed. Since May’s regional election, it has been governed by a coalition of the conservative People’s Party (PP) and Vox, once a fringe party that has drawn support by championing migrant deportations and tapping into a wider wave of far-right, anti-establishment support across Europe.
Ahead of Sunday’s snap vote, observers say Andalusia’s political dynamics could offer a glimpse of what might come next nationally.
That arrangement could soon be tested at the national level.
Opinion polls put the PP first, followed by Sanchez’s Socialists (PSOE), with Vox third.
The PP is projected to fall short of an outright majority, but together the two right-wing parties are expected to have enough seats to govern.
PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo has indicated that he would prefer to lead a minority government with Vox’s backing in parliament, while leaving open the possibility of a coalition like the one in Andalusia.
Tucked away between rows of greenhouses and arid mountains in the southern region of Andalusia, Rioja is home to about 1,600 people.
Overlooking the plains framing the quaint village is a giant silhouette of a bull. For much of Francisco Franco’s dictatorship , this area remained poor and largely agricultural.
As machines took over more of the work in the fields, many Andalusians left for jobs in industrial centres such as Barcelona and Madrid. In the mid-seventies, the Socialists found fertile ground in a society that had long felt marginalised and neglected.
In 1982, the PSOE won an absolute majority in Andalusia’s first regional election, beginning a stretch in power that lasted more than three decades.
But by 2018, the Socialists’ hold on the southern region was starting to crack.
A series of corruption scandals tarnished the party’s image, benefitting the PP. The PSOE still came first in that year’s regional election, but the conservatives took power with the backing of the liberal Ciudadanos and Vox.
“For the first time, the PP opened the door to the far-right to be able to govern – that created a precedent for everything that happens today nationwide,” said Bosco Govantes, political science associate professor at Sevilla’s Universidad Pablo de Olavide. “Before, there was a red line, a stigma, over collaborating with the far right. But that move in Andalusia kicked off the normalisation of Vox’s narrative.”
The party was founded in 2013 when a group of ultraconservatives, led by Santiago Abascal, broke up with the conservatives they accused of being too indulgent towards Catalan separatists.
Vox at first struggled to get into the political mainstream, but entered Andalusia’s regional parliament in 2018.
Once the Catalan issue faded from the national debate, the party shifted its focus to migration.
Abascal accuses Sanchez of enabling what he calls “a migrant invasion” to “replace the Spanish people” as the Socialist government adopted an open-door policy and legalised undocumented migrants who had worked in Spain for years.
Since the start of Sanchez’s rule to last year, the number of foreign-born residents in Spain rose from 6.3 million to 10.4 million, official figures show. He takes pride in the policy, as Spain’s GDP grew under his tenure.
Vox, the likely kingmaker that is expected to increase its vote share more than any other party compared with the 2023 elections, wants to reverse those policies.
Some observers say the conservative party has had to harden its discourse, such as calling for stricter measures against migrants, to stop haemorrhaging voters to its right.
Polling by Ipsos suggested up to 20 percent of Spaniards who voted for the PP in the 2023 elections intended to vote for Vox on Sunday.
Sanchez has pitched the election as a battle between progress and regression, warning that PP and Vox “only agree when it comes to cutting back rights”.
But that argument falls flat in parts of Andalusia, where some do not fear a Vox-PP deal.
“I don’t mind if Vox is in government,” said Rosaria, a 69-year-old retired housewife, while adjusting her white scarf with a red floral pattern. “The PP will keep them in check. It’s a party with vision and structure”.
Sanchez warns that Vox wants to roll back women’s rights.
The issue of gender violence divides the two parties.
Last year, the PP backed the renewal of Spain’s cross-party pact on gender-based violence.
Vox wants to repeal the 2004 gender-based violence law, which protects women from abuse by current or former partners. The party argues that the law discriminates against men and wants to replace it with legislation covering domestic violence regardless of the victim’s sex.
At an event against gender-based violence, Rioja’s PP mayor Olga Maria Gonzalez Jurado was asked how the two parties were getting on in government in Andalusia.
“I think it’s going well,” she said, but she deflected questions on whether the PP had hardened its stance on immigration to keep up with Vox.
In Andalusia, the two parties have been pushing for stricter housing rules for non-Spanish applicants.
Councils can already give people who live or work locally priority for subsidised housing, regardless of nationality. Last month, the two parties backed a non-binding motion urging Madrid to give Spanish citizens priority for subsidised housing and housing aid. Their regional coalition deal also pledges to give people with longstanding ties to Andalusia or Spain priority for public benefits and social housing.
In other regions, the two parties’ cooperation has reached classrooms and places of worship. Aragon dropped a school programme teaching Arabic and Moroccan culture this year and Andalusia is due to follow in 2027.
In the Murcia town of Jumilla, Muslims held Eid al-Fitr prayers in a car park after PP and Vox backed restrictions on the use of municipal sports facilities. The restrictions have drawn criticism over their impact on Muslim religious gatherings.
In Valencia, the parties backed a rule requiring meat served in school canteens to come from animals stunned before slaughter, which still allows halal meals that meet the requirement. In the Balearic Islands, they voted to send Spain’s Congress a bill to ban the burqa [full-face veils sometimes worn by Muslim women that hide the entire face, including eyes] and niqab [similar, but the eyes are visible] in public spaces.
Vox has called for the deportation of foreigners it says, among other grounds, also live on public benefits. This measure – to remove someone with a valid right to stay – has no equivalent in Europe.
The party’s policies have left migrants on edge.
Yudy Ramirez is from Colombia and entered Spain four years ago. For years, took care of her child while juggling two jobs as an in-house caregiver and fruit picker at a greenhouse in Almeria for five euros per hour.
In June, the 49-year-old finally received legal papers.
“Many of us are scared, because returning is not in the plans at the moment,” she said.
Still, not all migrants are targeted in the same way.
Vox’s rhetoric has an ethno-racial undertone which looks at Spanish-speaking foreigners coming from Latin America in more favourable terms as they belong to an Iberosphere which connects far-right movements in the Latin world whose centre is occupied by Vox.

Andalusia, Spain – Surrounded by shelves heaving with canned goods and cured meats, the owners of a family-run grocery store are locked in a debate about Spain’s upcoming elections.
All politicians are “liars”, proclaims 32-year-old Antonio Cerezo, announcing he will cast a blank ballot. His cousin, Patricia Nicolas Cerezo, 43, is less certain, riddled with doubt about who to support.
As for her 18-year-old son, first-time voter Alfonso Duque, the only choice is the far-right Vox party : “It can’t get worse than this”.
The one thing that the family in the small village of Rioja seems to agree on is that Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s socialists must go.
A former socialist bastion, the southern region’s political landscape has changed. Since May’s regional election, it has been governed by a coalition of the conservative People’s Party (PP) and Vox, once a fringe party that has drawn support by championing migrant deportations and tapping into a wider wave of far-right, anti-establishment support across Europe.
Ahead of Sunday’s snap vote, observers say Andalusia’s political dynamics could offer a glimpse of what might come next nationally.
That arrangement could soon be tested at the national level.
Opinion polls put the PP first, followed by Sanchez’s Socialists (PSOE), with Vox third.
The PP is projected to fall short of an outright majority, but together the two right-wing parties are expected to have enough seats to govern.

But that move in Andalusia kicked off the normalisation of Vox’s narrative.”

articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio was “particularly angry” when he learned of Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia’s CEO , having previously warned the Trump administration he was involved with a suspected Chinese spy , a report claims.
Huang made a dramatic comeback to the chipmaker powering the global AI boom Monday, less than two weeks after resigning over the alleged affair.
It subsequently emerged both President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance had played a pivotal role in convincing the tech company’s board of directors to take him back over the weekend, insisting only Huang could restore market confidence in Nvidia .
CBS News reports that neither Rubio nor CIA Director John Ratcliffe were part of the administration’s discussions about Huang’s return.
This reportedly left Rubio incensed because earlier this year he had prepared a classified memorandum warning about the alleged affair with a Megaspeed executive accused of funneling Nvidia’s chips to China.
CBS cites allies of Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent as saying the two men had “expressed private concern about aspects of Huang’s return,” although neither has criticised the decision in public.
Rubio has yet to comment on the scandal , despite being asked by reporters whether Huang posed a security risk. The Independent has reached out to the State Department and Treasury for comment.
Bessent, for his part, originally advised Nvidia to look “outside” for a new CEO, only to then row back on that position slightly during an appearance on CBS’s Face the Nation Sunday, when he told anchor Margaret Brennan: “Jensen is on the outside now.”
He has also criticized another Cabinet member not involved in Trump’s strategizing for Haung’s return, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, for failing to do enough to stop China obtaining advanced semiconductor chips or blacklist Megaspeed before this week.
Huang’s return initially caused Nvidia’s stock price to soar more than 30 percent Monday, leading to fresh accusations of the president enriching himself through his actions in public office given his large shareholding in the firm, which the White House has denied.
The market rebound proved short-lived , however, with the company dropping in value 5.9 percent Tuesday and 5 percent Wednesday, prompting the president to lash out against a New York Times journalist who pointed it out.
Huang was meanwhile welcomed back by employees at Nvidia’s California headquarters, where he promised to be “a better CEO the second time.” He will appear before House and Senate committees in Washington, D.C., next week to take questions from lawmakers on export controls, Chinese chip smuggling and national security.
Rubio’s political stock has risen since November’s crushing midterms defeat for Republicans , causing him to pull ahead of Vance in a recent Emerson poll of possible 2028 GOP presidential contenders.
The secretary previously said he will not run for the White House against the VP but has impressed supporters of late with his answers on the recent spate of tech outages and by managing to remain largely untarnished by the deeply-unpopular Iran war.

articles.title_orig: Trump tells Putin to ‘pull back all military aggression’ as he tries for peace deal to end ‘complete bloodbath’ in Ukraine
articles.title_zh: Trump tells Putin to ‘pull back all military aggression’ as he tries for peace deal to end ‘complete bloodbath’ in Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON — President Trump revealed he asked Vladimir Putin to stop all “military aggression”  in Europe in order to achieve a peace deal with Ukraine.
The president made the request when he met with the Russian president in China last week.
“I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe, in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine and made quickly,” Trump wrote on Truth Social Thursday morning of his historic sit-down with the Russian leader.
“I really believe this is a strong possibility,” he added. “Thousands of people are being killed each and every month, A COMPLETE BLOODBATH — and will be a Great Tribute to everyone!”
The president’s post offers the most detailed information to date about the discussion he had with Putin when the two sat down with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China.
After the meeting, Moscow ramped up its attacks on Ukraine, targeting its energy infrastructure as winter is settling in.
The statement also comes after Trump met with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte at Mar-a-Lago on Wednesday night. The two men issued a joint statement urging Russia to avoid actions that could expand the war with Ukraine.
“We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible,” Trump and Rutte said in their statement.
European leaders worry that Putin’s aggression could leave their countries a target for his military.
The concerns were compounded last week when Russian missiles entered Poland’s airspace. Polish leadership called it an “intentional ⁠provocation” by Moscow.
Great meeting with @POTUS It’s clearer than ever that American leadership remains essential as we build a stronger Europe in a stronger NATO https://t.co/1yciLroerD pic.twitter.com/HNHG35akre
“We know that what landed on Polish soil came from Russia. Therefore — ⁠and this is not just my own assessment, but ‌also that of our foreign partners, including those within NATO — it does not look like an ‌accident,” Prime Minister ⁠Donald Tusk said. “It ‌appears that we ⁠are dealing with an intentional ⁠provocation.”
Some European leaders saw Moscow’s move as an “escalation.”
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the Kremlin was “escalating” threats to European security, adding that “Russia knows exactly what it wants. And Russia wants more than Ukraine.”
Rutte said the NATO alliance is discussing how it would counter such a move.
“These latest Russian missiles need only five minutes longer to reach Lisbon, Rome or The Hague, my hometown, than to reach Tallinn, Warsaw or Helsinki,” Rutte told the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin on Monday.
“We face great dangers coming from Russia and the fact that Russia works so closely together with Iran, China, and North Korea, we know that Russia’s war machine at the moment is running at full speed,” he said.
Ukraine has long desired to join NATO but Russia, in the past, has objected. Trump also has expressed reservations.
But now Russia and Trump are comfortable with Article Five-style security guarantees for Ukraine, US envoy Jared Kushner revealed over the weekend.
NATO’s Article Five states that when one member of the alliance is attacked, all members will respond.
Kushner, after another round of peace talks, said Moscow is now “comfortable” with the idea, as is Trump.
“From America’s perspective, giving an Article 5-like security guarantee is a really, really big deal and I think that that is something that President Trump is open to, but obviously it has to be in America’s interest to do that,” Kushner said.

articles.title_orig: UK to get ‘Swiss-style’ consultative rights under new EU deals
articles.title_zh: UK to get ‘Swiss-style’ consultative rights under new EU deals
articles.content_orig:
The government and the EU have published the texts of two treaties agreed last week as part of a post-Brexit reset.
The treaties were published on Thursday afternoon, alongside legislation designed to enact the bulk of the deal.
The deal covering food exports has a 10-year termination clause that would mean if one party ended the agreement, they would have to pay "reasonable and proportionate costs" to rebuild border checks infrastructure, which will be significantly scaled back as part of the new deal.
Opposition leader Kemi Badenoch has said she would scrap the deal while Reform UK's Nigel Farage has suggested he would refuse to pay.
The Brexit reset deal has already sparked debate about its benefits, its costs, and a wider discussion on the future of the UK-EU relationship.
The deal covers British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme.
Two of the three legal texts were released on Thursday, covering the food trade and emissions trading scheme deals, alongside the government's cost-cutting bill to enact the deal.
A new assessment of the impact of the deal on different sectors and regions of the country was also released.
Under the deal, food exporters will be significant beneficiaries from the scrapping of considerable red tape and checks, and dismantling of border facilities. An internal analysis forecasts a 16% boost the export of major agricultural commodities.
The industry and government hope the reduction in costs for food producers and sellers will be passed on to customers, but there may be no clear visible impact at the checkout.
Privately, industry insiders told the BBC earlier this week that there are too many moving parts in the world economy, in particular the energy price shock resulting from war in the Middle East.
Regarding the fine detail in the text of one of the treaties relating to the 10-year termination clause, European affairs minister Hamish Falconer said: "The Cutting Costs Bill allows us to implement two major trade agreements."
"It allows us to eliminate paperwork for our food and drink traders, protect billions of pounds worth of British exports from carbon taxes, and make doing business with our largest trading partner cheaper and easier."
A plan to link British and European emissions trading schemes will see more coverage across the UK's aviation and maritime industries.
The treaty text also contains finer detail of how the UK will observe, shape but not vote on relevant EU rules. The UK will be invited to attend European Commission meetings and expert groups as an observer, as well as taking part in emergency food security planning.
However, the UK will not be given voting rights.
Plans to use secondary legislation, including granting direct so-called "Henry VIII powers" to ministers to align UK and EU laws, are detailed in the legislation.
Such powers will enable ministers to make changes to bills with less Parliamentary scrutiny.
Outlining the agreement with the EU to MPs earlier this week , the prime minister said new agreements with the EU are "pragmatic" and "not a prelude to anything".
Andy Burnham also said it would be "unthinkable" for the UK to rejoin the bloc without a referendum.
Several former prime ministers have urged him not to reopen the Brexit debate. Burnham said they are "stuck in the past" and later claimed there would be "no banging on about Europe" from Labour.
Badenoch said Burnham has "oversold" the deal and was "trying to take Britain back to 2015".
